Issued at 313 PM CDT Fri Oct 9 2026

REST OF TODAY AND TONIGHT:

Surface high pressure over the central Great Lakes as of Friday
afternoon has led to southeast winds with gusts to around 15-25 
mph and mostly clear skies across much of the Northland, though 
cloudier in far northern Minnesota to the Apostle Islands. 
Temperatures have warmed nicely away from Lake Superior into the
60s to around 70F aside from 50s for portions of the Arrowhead 
due to onshore flow. High temperatures top out in the 60s to 
even low 70s away from Lake Superior later this afternoon, 
highest in east-central Minnesota to inland northwest 
Wisconsin. Southeasterly winds continue into tonight, though 
wind gusts should drop off a bit. Look for low temperatures 
ranging ranging from the mid 50s in southwestern areas to 
mid/upper 40s in the Minnesota Arrowhead and parts of north- 
central Wisconsin. No precipitation is expected.

THIS WEEKEND:

On Saturday, an anomalous upper-level ridge axis centered just 
to our east and troughing over the Pacific Northwest will leave
the Northland nestled in between with southwest flow aloft. At 
the same time, surface low pressure in the Dakotas will leave a
tight pressure gradient out ahead of it extending into the 
Northland. This pressure gradient will bring summer-like warmth 
and gusty conditions into the Northland. High temperature 
forecasts for Saturday have remained consistent, reaching the 
upper 70s to mid-80s, warmest in the I-35 corridor to northwest 
Wisconsin. Downsloping southerly winds/compressional warming 
along the South Shore should boost temperatures there, but lead 
to onshore winds and cooler temperatures for the tip of the 
Arrowhead. Wind gusts of 25-35 mph are expected, as well as 
minimum relative humidity dipping to the 30s (%) in the warmest 
areas and upper 30s to 40s (%) elsewhere. These min RH forecasts
have been pretty consistent over the last 12-24 hours. The 
combination of fairly low relative humidity combined with the 
very warm and gusty conditions will likely lead to elevated to 
near- critical fire weather conditions on Saturday, particularly
in areas along/south of the Iron Range where winds and gusts 
will be stronger. We stay in the warm sector of the low pressure
system on Saturday night with gusty southerly winds continuing 
but gradually starting to weaken from NW to SE. This will keep 
low temperatures for many areas near daily record warm values in
the upper 50s to mid 60s, except mid-50s in far north- central 
Minnesota. Several locations are likely to approach and possibly
break record daily high temperatures for Saturday and record 
warm low temperatures for Saturday night (see the "Climate" 
section below).

The surface cold front associated with the aforementioned low 
pressure system will gradually be moving from northwest to 
southeast across the Northland on Sunday into Sunday night. 
The forecast progression of the front has been slightly slower
than previous forecasts, which should result in high 
temperatures around 80F into the mid-80s in Northwest Wisconsin
and as far west as east-central Minnesota and the Twin Ports.
Compressional warming from downslope winds into the South Shore
could also push Ashland's forecast high temperature into the
mid-80s, within a couple degrees of the record daily high for
Sunday. Most of northeast Minnesota should see highs in the 
70s, with some mid to upper 60s in far north-central Minnesota
behind the front. The warm temperatures, fairly low minimum RH,
and southerly wind gusts of 20-25 mph late Sunday morning and 
afternoon could lead to elevated fire weather conditions in
northwest Wisconsin, though potential is lower than on Saturday.

LATE SUNDAY INTO EARLY NEXT WEEK:

Upper-level support/troughing remains weak behind the cold 
front late Sunday, with light rain forecasts shifted slightly
farther north than yesterday's forecast. Far north-central 
Minnesota could see light rain chances arrive as early as late 
Sunday afternoon or evening, with rain chances then moving 
across areas along and north of the Iron Range Sunday evening 
and night, while areas farther south miss out on the initial 
round of rain. Areas that do see rain likely see less than 
only a few hundredths of an inch at best. 

Another trough aloft moves through the area Monday into Monday 
night as a secondary surface low moves across south-central Wisconsin
into the central Great Lakes. This will bring scattered, light 
rain chances to more of the Northland. However, additional
amounts remain light, ranging from a few hundredths in the
Brainerd Lakes into far inland northwest Wisconsin to 0.1-0.25"
along and north of the US HWY 2 corridor. Rainfall exits to the
east by early Tuesday morning.

More seasonal October temperatures for most return Monday and 
Tuesday, with upper 50s to around 70F in the southern half and 
50s in the northern half of the Northland. Lows Monday night are
forecast to drop into the low to mid 30s north
